reference.source: Robbins Basic Pathology 9th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Congo red apple green birefringence identifies amyloid
Thick heart walls with low ECG voltage mean infiltrative amyloid until proven otherwise
AL follows a plasma cell clone; AA follows chronic inflammation
Macroglossia and periorbital purpura favour AL type
reference.pathophysiology: Soluble precursor proteins misfold into insoluble beta pleated fibrils that deposit in extracellular matrix, increasing stiffness and disrupting function. Light chains, serum amyloid A, transthyretin and beta 2 microglobulin are the major precursors, each with distinct organ tropism.
additionalDifferentials: AL versus AA versus transthyretin amyloidosis
additionalInvestigations: Congo red staining of fat pad or organ biopsy with polarised microscopy
Serum free light chains and protein electrophoresis
Echocardiography with strain imaging and cardiac MRI
